title: Personal details and home address
purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete home address (as on the first working day), plus the canton for the pension fund. Residents of Switzerland choose their canton; for employees abroad Zurich is recorded and the canton is not asked.

stories.title: Collect the employee's name and date of birth
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the first step 'About you' of the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the registration at Pensionskasse Muster is never blocked by an empty required field (First name, Last name, Date of birth), and HR can identify the employee and address documents to them
stories.priority_reason: The pension fund portal rejects a registration when First name, Last name or Date of birth is empty, so without them the registration is blocked.

acceptance_criteria.title: First and last name are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 1 'About you' of the questionnaire (the step also holds the first working day, which another story covers), whatever they answer elsewhere
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to continue without a first name or a last name
acceptance_criteria.then: they cannot continue until both are filled in. The first and last name are recorded for the pension fund (its required fields 'First name' and 'Last name') and for HR, which uses the name to identify the employee and address documents. HR's need for the name is inferred: HR confirmed 'name, address' but only explained the address.

examples.name: Employee living abroad: name required too

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is always asked and required, as DD.MM.YYYY
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 1 'About you'
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is required for every employee and is given as a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.03.1990). It is recorded for the pension fund, whose registration form requires 'Date of birth' in that form.

examples.name: Any employee: date of birth required

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth must be plausible for the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has entered a date of birth and a first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the date of birth means they would be younger than 14 or older than 100 on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is not accepted and the employee is asked to correct it. An employee who is at least 14 and at most 100 years old on the first working day can continue. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-050): these age limits are a product decision, not stated by the pension fund or HR.

acceptance_criteria.title: No further personal identifiers are asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 1 'About you'
acceptance_criteria.when: they look at the questions in the step
acceptance_criteria.then: besides the first working day, only first name, last name and date of birth are asked. No social insurance (AHV) number and no badge photo are asked, because no receiving party in scope needs them.

stories.title: Collect a complete postal home address
stories.i_want: every new employee to give a complete postal home address (street, house number, postcode, town and country) as it will be on their first working day, in step 2 'Home address'
stories.so_that: the many documents HR posts to employees reach them, without HR having to chase missing parts of the address
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and states the address 'has to be complete'; an incomplete address stops HR's postal correspondence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Street, postcode and town are required for every employee
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address', wherever they live
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to continue with the street, the postcode or the town empty
acceptance_criteria.then: they cannot continue until street, postcode and town are filled in. The address is recorded for HR. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-049): every home address field is required; the only exception is the explicit 'no house number' option.

acceptance_criteria.title: House number is required, with an explicit 'no house number' option
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to continue without a house number
acceptance_criteria.then: they can continue only if they have entered a house number or explicitly chosen 'no house number'; an empty house number alone is not accepted. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-042): HR wants the address complete including the number, and some addresses have no house number.

examples.name: House number required for any employee

acceptance_criteria.title: The address is the one that applies on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee will move before their first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the question makes clear that the address asked is the one that applies on the first working day, so the employee enters their new address. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-041).

acceptance_criteria.title: Only a normal postal address is asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.when: they look at the address questions
acceptance_criteria.then: only what is needed to write the address on an envelope is asked: street, house number, postcode, town and country. Nothing else, such as a second address or a phone number, is asked.

stories.title: Use the home address country as the country of residence
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to count as their country of residence, without a separate residence question
stories.so_that: Lonio knows whether the employee lives in Switzerland or abroad. Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax, and the country decides which later questions apply. The employee is asked for the country only once.
stories.priority_reason: The country of residence decides source tax liability and the canton for the pension fund; without it neither the tariff nor the registration can be completed.

acceptance_criteria.title: Country is required and chosen from the country list
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.when: they give the country of their home address as it applies on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the country is required and is chosen from the ISO 3166 country list, shown by English name (e.g. Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein). This country is the employee's country of residence; no separate question about the country of residence is asked. It is recorded for HR as part of the postal address, for source tax and for the pension fund (the fund uses it to decide the canton). Assumptions to be verified by a domain expert: the country list (D-050) and the address as on the first working day (D-041).

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are subject to source tax and are not asked nationality or canton
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality (HR's example: Stefan is Swiss, lives abroad and is still subject). Their nationality is not asked (data minimisation), and the canton is not asked either. 'Here' in HR's rule is read as Switzerland; assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-043).

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss, living abroad (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a; country assumed)

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland are asked their nationality and canton
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked their canton of residence in step 2 and their nationality in step 3 'Nationality and C permit'. Whether they are subject to source tax then depends on those later answers, not on the country alone.

stories.title: Ask Swiss residents for their canton
stories.i_want: a canton for every new employee: the canton of residence chosen by employees who live in Switzerland, and Zurich (the canton of the place of work at Muster AG) for employees who live abroad, without asking them
stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the registration is always filled, even for employees living abroad, for whom the fund's list has no option
stories.priority_reason: 'Canton' is a required field of the fund's registration; if it is empty the registration is rejected ('Canton is required.').

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland choose their canton
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked their canton of residence, it is required, and they choose one of the 26 cantons the fund lists: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich. The chosen canton is recorded as the canton for the pension fund.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are not asked; Zurich is recorded
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton is not asked, and Zurich, the canton of the place of work at Muster AG, is recorded as the canton for the pension fund. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-002): the fund's portal does not say whether 'Canton' means residence or place of work, and its list has no option for a residence abroad.

acceptance_criteria.title: The canton for the fund always follows the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: the questionnaire has been submitted and HR later changes the employee's country of residence
acceptance_criteria.when: the canton for the pension fund is derived again
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows the latest answers. If the employee now lives abroad, Zurich is recorded and any canton chosen earlier is discarded. If the employee now lives in Switzerland but no canton was ever asked, the canton for the fund shows 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters it. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-048). How HR makes the change belongs to the later HR-side spec.
